answer: Shared-fate pooling: the node logs, per key, which epochs it went silent or lagged. Keys whose outages coincide above 0.9 over 20 epochs are merged into one payee, since a farm on one host hits its nadir together. Pool 1,000 POA, 100 honest keys: 50 sybils on one box, merged, earn 1000/101 = 9.9 POA instead of 50/150 x 1000 = 333. Escaping means 50 truly independent hosts and uptime, about $250/month at $5 each, a real per-head cost. Every downtime record stays a relic on-ledger, so one shared thread of failures exposes the cluster later.
